newsitem.title: USA: Giant Food says new pact to save money.
newsitem.headline: Giant Food says new pact to save money.

text.p: Giant Food Inc said the the four-and-a-half-year contract ratified Sunday by its Teamsters-represented drivers will save the company at least $300,000 per year in operating costs and will free the company to use outside drivers.

In a telephone interview, Giant Senior Vice President and General Counsel David Rutstein said the grocery industry in the last several decades has seen more and more companies use outside warehouses and drivers to deliver products directly to grocery stores.
"This new agreement gives us the opportunity to take advantage of those alternative methods," Rutstein said.
The new pact is expected to save at least $300,000 a year in wages and benefits alone, he said.
The 320 Teamsters-represented drivers that struck the company from December 14 until Sunday will be phased back into work over the next several days, Rutstein said.

He said the union accepted settlement by a 247 to 24 vote Sunday. The strike closed two of the company's warehouses in Landover and Jessup, Md.; a bakery in Silver Spring, Md; and a dairy in Landover, Rutstein said.
"But all of our 175 stores operated throughout the period," he said.
